config.title: Scale, Load & Bottlenecks

intro.title: Scale, Load & Bottlenecks
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple simulation of a web server to understand how system performance changes under different loads. You'll learn the core concepts of scale (handling more requests), load (the amount of traffic), and bottlenecks (the slowest parts that limit performance). The main technologies involved are basic system modeling and performance metrics. By the end, you'll be able to identify and analyze bottlenecks in a system design scenario.
intro.usecase: Understanding scale, load, and bottlenecks is essential for building reliable systems that handle real-world traffic. When an e-commerce site like Amazon experiences a flash sale, engineers must anticipate traffic spikes and identify database bottlenecks before checkout systems fail. Similarly, social media platforms like Instagram must scale their image processing pipelines to handle millions of uploads during peak hours without degrading user experience. As a developer, you'll apply these concepts when designing APIs that serve thousands of concurrent requests or optimizing database queries that slow down admin dashboards under heavy load.

objectives: Construct a basic load balancer simulation to distribute incoming requests
Configure a monitoring dashboard to visualize system performance metrics
Implement a caching layer to reduce database load for frequently accessed data
Apply horizontal scaling techniques by adding server instances to handle increased traffic
Manipulate request rates to simulate different load conditions and observe system behavior
Initialize a bottleneck detection mechanism that triggers alerts when thresholds are exceeded
Integrate auto-scaling rules that automatically adjust resources based on predefined metrics

steps.title: Define core concepts: Scale, Load, and Bottlenecks
steps.instruction: Create three constant variables to define: 1) Scale (ability to handle growth), 2) Load (demand on system), and 3) Bottlenecks (performance constraints).
steps.hint: Use the const keyword followed by a descriptive variable name and assign it a string definition.
steps.analogousExample:
// Defining a concept variable
const reliability = 'The probability a system performs correctly under specified conditions for a given time interval.';
steps.seedCode: // Define three constant variables for Scale, Load, and Bottlenecks
steps.expectedOutcome: Three constant variables are created with definitions for Scale, Load, and Bottlenecks.
successCriteria: Variables named scale, load, and bottlenecks are defined with appropriate string definitions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined some concepts, but make sure you have all three: Scale, Load, and Bottlenecks.
steps.feedbackWrong: The definitions are missing or incorrect. Create three constant variables with clear definitions.

steps.title: Initialize system metrics state
steps.instruction: Create an object named 'systemMetrics' to store initial system performance metrics. The object should have these properties: requestsPerSecond, responseTime, errorRate, and activeUsers.
steps.hint: Define a constant variable using 'const' and assign it an object with the specified properties. You can set initial values to 0 or any reasonable starting numbers.
steps.seedCode:
// Define three constant variables for Scale, Load, and Bottlenecks

// Create systemMetrics object here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a systemMetrics object ready to track key performance indicators for system scaling analysis.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the systemMetrics object, but it's missing some required properties. Make sure to include requestsPerSecond, responseTime, errorRate, and activeUsers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The systemMetrics object wasn't created correctly. You need to define a constant variable named 'systemMetrics' that contains an object with the four specified properties for tracking system performance.

steps.title: Create load simulation function
steps.instruction: Define a function named simulateLoad that increases requestsPerSecond by 50 and activeUsers by 100 each time it's called.
steps.hint: Create a function that modifies the systemMetrics object's requestsPerSecond and activeUsers properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A simulateLoad function that increments requestsPerSecond by 50 and activeUsers by 100.
successCriteria: The simulateLoad function is defined and correctly modifies both requestsPerSecond and activeUsers properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it increments both requestsPerSecond by 50 and activeUsers by 100.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named simulateLoad that increases both metrics.

steps.title: Create bottleneck detection function
steps.instruction: Define a function named detectBottleneck that takes systemMetrics as a parameter and returns a string describing any detected bottleneck.
steps.hint: Create a function that checks if responseTime exceeds a threshold (e.g., 500ms) or if errorRate is too high (e.g., > 5%). Return a descriptive message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A detectBottleneck function is defined that analyzes systemMetrics and returns a string describing any performance bottleneck.
successCriteria: The detectBottleneck function is defined, takes systemMetrics as a parameter, and returns a string based on responseTime or errorRate thresholds.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it takes systemMetrics as a parameter and returns a descriptive string based on threshold checks.
steps.feedbackWrong: The bottleneck detection function isn't properly defined. Create a function named detectBottleneck that analyzes systemMetrics for performance issues.

steps.title: Create scaling decision function
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'makeScalingDecision' that takes the current load and bottleneck status as parameters and returns a scaling decision string.
steps.hint: Create a function that checks if there's a bottleneck and high load, then returns an appropriate scaling recommendation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that analyzes load and bottleneck data to determine when scaling is needed.
successCriteria: Function 'makeScalingDecision' is defined with parameters and returns a scaling decision string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes parameters and returns a decision string.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named 'makeScalingDecision' that returns scaling recommendations based on load and bottleneck status.

steps.title: Build system dashboard structure
steps.instruction: Create a function named renderDashboard that returns a container div with three sections: one for Current Metrics, one for Load Simulation, and one for System Status. Use placeholder headings for each section.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns a div element containing three separate divs or sections with appropriate headings.
steps.expectedOutcome: A renderDashboard function that returns a container with three section placeholders for system monitoring.
successCriteria: Function renderDashboard is defined and returns a div containing three sections with headings for Current Metrics, Load Simulation, and System Status.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You have the function, but make sure it returns a div with exactly three sections containing the required headings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dashboard structure isn't complete. Create a function that returns a container with three sections for Current Metrics, Load Simulation, and System Status.

steps.title: Display current system metrics
steps.instruction: Inside the dashboard structure function, add a <div> element that displays the current values of requestsPerSecond, responseTime, errorRate, and activeUsers from the systemMetrics object.
steps.hint: Access the properties of the systemMetrics object (e.g., systemMetrics.requestsPerSecond) and display them within JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboard will show real-time system metrics including requests per second, response time, error rate, and active users.
successCriteria: A <div> element is added inside the SystemDashboard component that displays all four systemMetrics properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some metrics, but make sure to display all four: requestsPerSecond, responseTime, errorRate, and activeUsers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metrics display wasn't added correctly. Check that you're accessing the systemMetrics object properties and displaying them within JSX.

steps.title: Add load simulation controls
steps.instruction: Inside the SystemDashboard component, add a button element with the text 'Simulate Load Increase' that calls the simulateLoad function when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a button with an onClick handler that invokes the simulateLoad function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Simulate Load Increase' appears in the dashboard, which will trigger the load simulation function when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element with the text 'Simulate Load Increase' is present in the SystemDashboard component and has an onClick handler that calls simulateLoad.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it calls the simulateLoad function when clicked and has the correct label.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't properly trigger the load simulation. Check the onClick handler and button text.

steps.title: Add scaling action button
steps.instruction: Add a button inside your SystemDashboard component that calls the makeScalingDecision function when clicked and displays the scaling decision result.
steps.hint: Add a button element with an onClick handler that calls makeScalingDecision. You can display the result in a paragraph or div.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button that triggers scaling decisions appears in the dashboard, allowing users to see how the system responds to performance bottlenecks.
successCriteria: The SystemDashboard component contains a button with onClick handler calling makeScalingDecision and displays the scaling decision result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it needs to properly call the makeScalingDecision function when clicked and display the result. Make sure the onClick handler is correctly set up.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scaling action button is missing or not properly implemented. Add a button element with onClick={makeScalingDecision} inside the SystemDashboard component.
